questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: The history of English folk dancing
How to become a professional dancer
Why dance classes are becoming so expensive in Britain
How dancing can benefit our brains and emotions
questions.why: Beth says they'll hear how dancing can benefit our brains and emotions at every stage of life.

questions.q: How does Neil feel about dancing?
options: He loves it and goes dancing every single week
He thinks it's a waste of time
He isn't very good and feels a bit embarrassed
He only dances at weddings
questions.why: He says he's not a great dancer and gets a bit embarrassed.

questions.q: Why does Julia Ravey love dancing?
options: It helps her get rid of stress
It is her job
It helps her lose weight
It lets her meet lots of new people
questions.why: She says it's a release she relies on “to get the stress out of my body”.

questions.q: What does Julia accept about other people?
options: Everyone secretly loves dancing
Some people find dancing awkward and avoid it
Most people she knows dance much better than she does
Older people shouldn't dance
questions.why: She says some people find dancing awkward and avoid the dance floor at all costs.

questions.q: What has Dr Peter Lovatt studied?
options: How dancing improves brain function in people of all ages
Why some people can't hear rhythm
How to cure Alzheimer's and Parkinson's with new medicines
The history of ballet and jazz
questions.why: For four decades he's studied how dancing helps brain function in children, adults and older people.

questions.q: What does Dr Lovatt's dance therapy involve?
options: Learning difficult steps from a teacher in a dance class
Dancing in large groups in public
Copying dance videos online
Moving freely with your eyes closed, led by the music
questions.why: It involves spontaneous movements, closing your eyes and letting the music move you.

questions.q: What is Dr Lovatt's first suggestion for people who don't dance?
options: Go to a nightclub with friends and watch them dance
Lie on your bed and feel the beat of music you like
Watch other people dancing first
Take a Morris dancing class
questions.why: He suggests lying on your bed with your eyes closed, listening to music and feeling the rhythm.

questions.q: What does Beth mean when she says “a dance a day keeps the doctor away”?
options: Doctors are now recommending dance classes to patients
Dancing too much can be dangerous
Dancing regularly can help keep you healthy
People who dance don't like doctors
questions.why: She's summarising the huge health benefits of dancing they've discussed.
